problem: Work on world models, video generation, model-based RL and VLA policies is scattered under different names. Predictive models and policies are often trained or deployed separately, and evaluation measures prediction quality and control quality in isolation.
motivation: Reactive VLA policies do not model how actions change future states, which hurts long-horizon, delayed-effect and contact-rich tasks. Standalone world models produce plausible futures that are not necessarily actionable. A unified robotics-oriented view of World-Action Models (WAMs) is needed to compare design choices and evaluation criteria.
key_idea: Define WAMs as models that couple future-state prediction with executable action generation, either by joint prediction or by plan-then-act with inverse dynamics, and organize the literature by a multi-axis taxonomy.
insight: The survey argues that neither joint prediction nor inverse-dynamics factorization is universally better, and that the main challenge is aligning pretrained video priors with embodiment-specific control. It also argues that world prediction and action selection have different natural objectives, so decoupled training may avoid a policy exploiting overly optimistic imagined states. As a survey it has no ablations of its own; these points come from cited works and the authors' analysis.
method: Definition and scope: formalizes WAMs on a POMDP, contrasting WM (z_{t+1}=f(z_t,a_t)), VLA (a=f(o,l)) and WAM (jointly predicts o_{t:t+H} and a_{t:t+H}), and decomposes them into policy, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics and visual planning.

Model components: language encoder (CLIP/T5/LLM), visual encoder (2D/video VAE, DINO/SigLIP/VJEPA, 3D/BEV, VLM), backbone (scratch transformer vs pretrained video foundation model), action decoder (tokenizer, latent action model, diffusion/flow head).
Transition paradigms: joint prediction (GR-1, UWM, WorldVLA, Motus, Cosmos Policy) vs inverse dynamics plan-then-act (Pathdreamer, Seer, DreamZero, LingBot-VA, Fast-WAM).
Architecture structures: end-to-end single-backbone systems vs dual systems that separate a world module and an action module via MoT routing or cross-attention (VPP, VidMan, pi0-style, Helix).

Training pipeline: pre-training (spatiotemporal representation, action representation, video-action alignment), then post-training (fine-tuning, data augmentation/synthetic trajectories, RL in imagined environments).
Data modality and scaling: language, multi-view video, 3D geometry, tactile/audio, proprioception; data pyramid from internet video to egocentric demos to embodied trajectories.

Applications and evaluation: manipulation, navigation, driving; tables of methods, datasets, benchmarks and metrics; challenges: alignment, factorization, 3D consistency, memory, neural simulators, latency.
numbers_note: Survey paper with no experimental results of its own; the tables only list methods, benchmarks and metric definitions.
results: No experiments. It contributes a taxonomy (joint prediction vs inverse dynamics; end-to-end vs dual system) and a catalog of WAMs across manipulation, navigation and driving. It identifies open challenges: action alignment, world-action factorization, spatial consistency, long-horizon memory, neural simulators, and inference efficiency.
limitations: Purely a literature review with no quantitative comparison of methods.
Navigation coverage is thin (about 9 methods, mostly look-ahead planning) and does not compare VLN benchmark results.
Definition of WAM is broad and partly overlaps with VLAs and model-based RL, so category boundaries are blurry.
